tts: The median salary in Switzerland is about seven thousand francs a month. That's roughly double its neighbors. So where does that money come from?
Secret number one: what they make. Medicines in Basel, banking in Zurich, watches in the Jura, commodity trading in Geneva. Expensive stuff, sold to the whole world.
Those companies pay a lot. So everyone else has to keep up: the waiter, the cashier, the bus driver. Otherwise, people just leave.
Secret number two: skills. About two thirds of teens skip university and do an apprenticeship instead, learning right on the job.
Secret number three: stability. A strong franc, neutrality, and low taxes in cantons like Zug. Big companies move their headquarters here.
But life is expensive too. Mandatory health insurance is about four hundred sixty francs a month. A two-bedroom in Zurich? Around three thousand.
So it's a chain: expensive products, high productivity, high wages, and high prices.
The Swiss aren't paid a lot out of generosity. Their work is simply worth a lot.
